ledger.note: Searched the Prosperity Line and Hope Gas. The sources describe a 30-mile line for the Monarch Compute Campus data center in Mason County, West Virginia. No source ties it to LNG.
Searched Questar's Southern System 2005 expansion. FERC and trade coverage tie it to deliveries at Goshen, Utah, for three shippers. No source ties it to LNG.
Searched Questar's Southern System expansion to Goshen. FERC coverage ties it to the Kern River interconnect at Goshen and three firm shippers. No source ties it to LNG.
Searched the Regency Intrastate Gas system. The sources describe a Louisiana intrastate line that delivers gas to downstream pipelines and markets. No source ties it to an LNG terminal's feedgas.
Searched the Regency Intrastate Gas system. The EIA entry for the Winnsboro extension gives no LNG link, and no other source found one.
Searched Renaissance Gas Transmission and Spectra. Found no coverage of this project. The LNG results concerned a Canadian terminal and its pipeline, which is not this line. No LNG tie.
Searched the Rendezvous lateral. The sources describe a Questar line from Black Forks to a Kern River interconnect in Wyoming. No source ties it to LNG.
Searched the Revolution Pipeline. Its gas goes into Rover, and its liquids go to Mariner East and Marcus Hook. Those liquids routes are not this gas line. No source ties this gas line to LNG.
EIA says the Risberg Line delivers to an Ohio utility for peak-day service and names no LNG link. I did not run a separate search on this line.
Searched the Rover Bulger and Harmon Creek expansion. The FERC filing shows Range Resources as the shipper and no LNG link. No source ties it to LNG.

Searched Rover. An RBN Energy flow-data article from around 2017 and 2018 shows some Rover gas reaching Sabine Pass indirectly through ANR. That is a system-level flow observation, not a source tying this Phase 1 line to LNG, so nothing is staged. Flagged for Baird.

Searched Rover. The same RBN flow-data article shows some Rover gas reaching Sabine Pass indirectly through ANR. It is a system-level observation, not a tie for this Phase 2 line, so nothing is staged. Flagged for Baird.

EIA says the Rover expansion needed no new construction to fix operating conditions on the mainline. Searched Rover and found no LNG tie for this expansion. The system flow article is not a tie for this line.
EIA says the Wick meter station adds takeaway capacity out of the Marcellus with a new Equitrans interconnection. No source ties it to LNG.

Searched the Ruby Pipeline. It carries Rockies gas from Opal, Wyoming, to Malin, Oregon. The Jordan Cove LNG supply was planned through a separate Pacific Connector line, not Ruby. No LNG tie for Ruby.
Searched Sabal Trail with LNG terms. The sources describe a Florida and Georgia line serving power and utility customers. No source ties Phase I to LNG.
EIA says Phase II delivers to Florida electric utilities. Searched Sabal Trail and found no LNG tie.
Searched Sabal Trail Phase III. It is a compressor upgrade for Florida and Georgia utility deliveries. No source ties it to LNG.
EIA says the Saginaw Trail line serves Detroit-area utility customers. I did not run a separate search. No LNG link appears in the entry or the existing refs.
Searched the Sandhills pipeline. Coverage describes a Progress Energy line to a North Carolina power plant. A separate Piedmont LNG storage plant is not tied to this line. No LNG tie.
